item.title: Demagnetization-Driven Nanoscale Chirality-Selective Phonon Transport
item.description: Chiral-lattice degrees of freedom can offer novel chirality-selective functionalities for thermotronic applications. Chiral phonons, which carry both heat and angular momentum, can arise from broken chiral degeneracy in phonon bands or from angular momentum transfer from photons or spins. Here, we demonstrate a nanoscale chirality-selective phonon transport based on a simple heterostructure of ferromagnetic [Co/Pt] multilayers and insulating chiral α-SiO(2). Using magneto-optic thermometry, we...

item.title: Silicate fertilizer mitigates methane emissions from rice paddies by enriching Burkholderia to modulate microbial interactions
item.description: Methane emissions from rice paddies are a major source of greenhouse gases, and silicate fertilizer (SF) derived from blast furnace slag has emerged as an environmentally friendly amendment that reduces methane release. SF modifies the soil redox environment by supplying electron acceptors such as iron, but the microbial mechanisms underlying methane mitigation remain unclear. Here, we combined metagenomic profiling, microbial isolation, and greenhouse experiments to show that SF consistently...

item.title: Position Over Composition: Positional Isomerism Enables Encapsulation-Independent Intrinsic Stability in a Conjugated Polymer
item.description: Conjugated polymers derive their optoelectronic function from π-delocalization. However, this feature renders them intrinsically susceptible to photochemical degradation. Here, we show that intrinsic stability can be altered without changing chemical composition by repositioning side chains. In polydiphenylacetylene derivatives, shifting substituents from the para to the meta position increases photostability by more than fivefold. This stability hierarchy, driven by positional isomerism rather...

item.title: Patterns of base chromosome numbers, genome size and rDNA loci evolution in the genus Capsicum (Solanaceae)
item.description: The size, organization and dynamics of the evolution of plant genomes vary widely among and within evolutionary lineages. The relatively small genus Capsicum provides an excellent system for studying genome evolution because all the species are diploid and possess one of two base chromosome numbers (x = 12 or 13). Here, we report chromosome numbers, genome sizes, and numbers of 5S and 35S rDNA loci for 24 Capsicum taxa representing eight of the nine currently recognized clades and one outgroup...

item.title: Chemical Functionality Engineering of Anti-Solvent Additives for Photostable Perovskite Solar Cells
item.description: Metal-halide perovskite solar cells (PSCs) achieve high power-conversion efficiencies but remain susceptible to photo-induced degradation caused by mobile ions and phase segregation. Here, we investigate positional isomers of pyridine-carboxylic acid, namely pyridine-2-carboxylic acid (2-PC) and pyridine-4-carboxylic acid (4-PC), as anti-solvent additives to clarify how functional-group orientation governs defect passivation and photo-induced degradation. Both additives improve film morphology...

item.title: Prevalence of Sarcopenia in Korean Adults Based on the Asian Working Group for Sarcopenia 2025 Criteria: Analysis of the 2024 Korea National Health and Nutrition Examination Survey
item.description: CONCLUSION: Application of the AWGS 2025 BMI-adjusted criteria identifies a substantial proportion of Korean older adults at risk of sarcopenia, with women aged ≥ 80 years particularly vulnerable. The divergence between BIA and DEXA measurements in very old adults suggests that measurement modality should be carefully considered in clinical practice. These findings provide timely evidence for public health planning as Korea enters a super-aged society.

item.title: Sex Hormone-Binding Globulin Limits Glucocorticoid-Induced Muscle Wasting by Preserving Estrogen-Dependent Repression of Catabolic Signaling
item.description: CONCLUSIONS: SHBG acts as a promoter of estrogen bioavailability that coordinates a protective endocrine crosstalk, counteracting GR-driven catabolism in female skeletal muscle. These findings identify SHBG as a key metabolic determinant and a promising therapeutic target to prevent corticosteroid-induced muscle wasting.

item.title: Fano-Engineered Au@Se Core-Shell Colloidal Pigments for Dual-Mode Structural Color
item.description: Colloidal structural colorants are attractive because they are substrate-free and solution-processable, but single-component plasmonic or dielectric colloids usually exhibit broad visible resonances that limit chroma. Here we report Au@Se core-shell colloidal pigments in which a plasmonic Au core is embedded within a visible-range Mie-resonant Se shell. The key signature is not the gradual red shift expected from passive dielectric loading, but an asymmetric hybrid feature with compressed...

item.title: Association Between Advance Care Planning and Place of Death: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis
item.description: BACKGROUND: Place of death is a key indicator of quality in end-of-life care, reflecting how well care aligns with patients' values and preferences. Advance care planning (ACP) has been proposed to support goal-concordant care, yet evidence regarding its association with actual place of death remains inconsistent.

item.title: Oncologic outcomes of sublobar resection in non-small cell lung cancer ≤3 cm with adverse pathologic features
item.description: CONCLUSIONS: Visceral pleural invasion, STAS, and high-grade histology were independently associated with recurrence, whereas resection extent was not. The weighted analysis did not show a clear separation between surgical groups, although the present analysis was not designed to demonstrate comparable efficacy between the two surgical approaches.

item.title: Phenotypic discovery of a benzopyranylpyrazole-based ferroptosis inhibitor that directly scavenges lipid radicals within phospholipid bilayers
item.description: Phenotypic screening against a diversity-oriented library identified a novel benzopyranylpyrazole core that suppresses ferroptosis. Optimization yielded SB3507, a selective, broad-spectrum inhibitor with nanomolar potency (IC(50) = 108 nM). Mechanistic studies and biomimetic liposome assays confirm that SB3507 partitions into lipid bilayers to directly terminate lipid radical chain reactions.

item.title: Empirical Understanding of Li-Ion Transport Through Hetero-Grain Boundaries Within Li-Electrolyte Interface for Stable Li Metal Anodes
item.description: Understanding the Li-ion transport mechanism across the Li/electrolyte interface (LEI) is fundamental for stabilizing Li-metal batteries (LMBs). In particular, hetero-grain boundaries (h-GBs) such as Li(2)O/LiF or Li(2)CO(3)/LiF are theoretically recognized to provide favorable Li-ion pathways within inorganic LEI; however, experimental verification of h-GB-mediated Li-ion transport remains elusive. In this study, we provide experimental evidence for favorable Li-ion transport associated with...

item.title: Engineering Carbon Nanotube Quantum Well Defects With Recognition Tripeptides for Optical Detection of Extracellular Vesicles in Plasma
item.description: Extracellular vesicles (EVs) carry surface proteins that reflect the molecular signatures of their originating cells. However, their low abundance and the modest sensitivity of current EV detection methods in complex biological environments limit access to EV surface biology in the native biological context. Here, we present a near-infrared optical nanosensor comprising a quantum well defect functionalized carbon nanotube coupled with integrin-recognition RGD tripeptide to detect surface...

item.title: Amorphous Dielectric-Integrated Retina-Inspired HfS<sub>2</sub> Devices with Enhanced Synaptic Plasticity for Neuromorphic Vision Assistance
item.description: Realizing neuromorphic functionalities in field-effect transistors (FETs) requires precise modulation of multilevel conductance states with robust retention. Two-dimensional (2D) semiconductor FETs, however, often suffer from a limited synaptic weight dynamic range and short retention times because of inadequate charge dynamics in the channel. This results from the low-k dielectric nature of the channel, which provides limited and unstable carrier storage sites and insufficient capacitive...

item.title: Bleeding With Asundexian Versus Placebo in Patients With Noncardioembolic Ischemic Stroke or High-Risk TIA: OCEANIC-STROKE Randomized Trial
item.description: CONCLUSIONS: Asundexian added to antiplatelet therapy reduced ischemic stroke without significantly increasing major, major or CRNM, or any bleeding. Lower gastrointestinal bleeding was more frequent with asundexian, whereas treatment effects on major and major or CRNM bleeding were consistent across prespecified subgroups.

item.title: Effectiveness of Negative Pressure Wound Therapies on the Healing Diabetic Foot Ulcer: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis
item.description: CONCLUSIONS: The findings of this study indicate that NPWT administered by nurses improves wound healing in DFU patients. Regarding infection control, this study did not produce statistically significant results.

item.title: The clinical course of nasal polyps in relation with histological and radiological findings
item.description: CONCLUSION: Eosinophilic NPs are associated with greater CT disease burden and extent. Peripheral eosinophil counts reflect tissue eosinophilia and correlate with radiologic severity.

item.title: Association between Cardiovascular Health by Life's Essential 8 and Subsequent Coronary Artery Calcium Score: The Cardiovascular and Metabolic Diseases Etiology Research Center Cohort
item.description: CONCLUSION: Our study showed that higher baseline CVH scores were associated with a lower risk of subsequent CAC, highlighting the importance of promoting ideal CVH early to reduce the burden of cardiovascular disease.

item.title: Vibroacoustic lung therapy and early postoperative oxygenation after cardiac surgery: a multicentre prospective study
item.description: CONCLUSION: VibroLUNG use was associated with a higher early postoperative P/F ratio and lower administered FiO₂. No adverse events, device deficiencies, or deaths were recorded during the study observation period. Causal inference is limited by the non-randomized design and centre-level differences.

item.title: Consensus recommendations for neurofibromatosis type 1 management in Asia Pacific
item.description: Neurofibromatosis type 1 (NF1) is a complex multisystem disorder requiring coordinated multidisciplinary care. This study aimed to develop consensus recommendations for NF1 management in the Asia-Pacific region. A modified Delphi process involving two survey rounds and a virtual meeting was conducted with experts from nine countries. A total of 141 statements were evaluated using a 9-point Likert scale with a 75% consensus threshold. Consensus was achieved across key domains including diagnosis,...

item.title: Mechanical macrocyclic effects: stimuli-responsive dual emission by self-inclusion and mutual exclusion
item.description: A macrocycle divides space into an inside and an outside. This physical boundary allows a guest to reside either within the cavity or outside. When two guests are tethered to one macrocycle, they compete for the same cavity and mutually exclude each other. We exploit this simple principle to design a macrocyclic molecular device with two identical fluorophores. By design, when one fluorophore pendant is sequestered by the nonpolar cavity ("in"), the other is automatically exposed to the polar...

item.title: Retinal organoid-based evaluation of icariin-loaded extracellular vesicles for hypoxia-induced retinal injury via mitochondrial modulation
item.description: CONCLUSION: These findings demonstrate that EV_ICA exerts neuroprotective effects by preserving mitochondrial quality control and restoring functional retinal gene programs under hypoxic stress. EV_ICA may therefore serve as a promising therapeutic candidate for hypoxia-related retinal degeneration and provide potential applications for cell-free regenerative medicine.

item.title: Gendered experiences of cause-specific unmet medical need: An intersectional analysis using MAIHDA
item.description: Unmet medical needs (UMN) persist even under universal health coverage and remain unequally distributed across social groups. Although gender differences in UMN are well documented, less is known about how gender intersects with family and work roles to shape healthcare access. We analyzed data from 230,925 adults aged ≥19 years in the 2024 Korea Community Health Survey. Outcomes were overall, time-related, and cost-related UMN. Multilevel Analysis of Individual Heterogeneity and Discriminatory...

item.title: Modulating protein-polysaccharide gel networks via almond protein to improve physicochemical stability of millet-based set yogurt
item.description: Low soluble protein content and poor gelation in millet milk compromise the formation of firm set yogurts. This study developed a millet-based set yogurt with improved physicochemical stability by incorporating almond protein isolate (API; 0-2%, w/v), which contributes a mild flavor, acid stability, and gel-forming capacity. API supplementation promoted acid-induced gelation via ionic interactions within the protein-polysaccharide matrix. Formulations with 0.5-1% API formed self-supporting gels...

item.description: Metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease affects roughly 38% of adults, yet approved agents do not correct the upstream redox-metabolic perturbations-a depressed nicotinamide adenine dinucleotide (NAD^(+)/NADH) ratio, saturated lipid excess, and endoplasmic reticulum (ER) stress-that drive hepatocyte injury. item.title: Minimalist d‑Tripeptide Prodrug Mimetics of the Myostatin Prodomain as Selective Inhibitors of Skeletal Muscle Atrophy Signaling
item.description: Skeletal muscle atrophy is driven in part by unrestrained myostatin (MSTN) signaling. We designed all-d tripeptide prodrug mimetics of the MSTN prodomain minimum active 23-mer fragment. Compounds 1 (H-d-Arg-d-Leu-d-Ala-OiPr) and 2 (H-d-Arg-d-Abu-d-Ala-OiPr) inhibited MSTN-induced myotube atrophy with sub-micromolar potency, while free-acid analogues (3, 4) and scrambled control (scr) were less active. All-d configuration conferred proteolytic stability exceeding 24 h. In vivo, compound 1...

item.title: Frequency, causes, and duration of drug shortages in South Korea, 2018-2024: a nationwide descriptive analysis of regulatory reporting data and temporal patterns across the COVID-19 pandemic
item.description: CONCLUSION: The patterns observed are consistent with structural vulnerabilities related to market incentives, regulatory processes, and API import dependence, with raw-material and demand-related causes becoming more prominent in the later study periods. Potential policy responses, each requiring separate evaluation, include supply diversification, domestic API production, cost-compensation for economically vulnerable essential medicines, and a risk-based early-warning system with...

item.title: Inhibitory effects of propyl paraben, citral, and gallic acid on the growth, patulin biosynthesis, and patulin biosynthetic gene expression of Penicillium paneum OM1
item.description: Penicillium paneum is a phytopathogen that can cause fruit decay and produce patulin in pears. Much information is not available about inhibitory effects of food-grade natural compounds on the patulin production by P. paneum and its growth. In this study, we evaluated the effects of propyl paraben, citral, and gallic acid on patulin accumulation by P. paneum OM1 and its growth on YES (patulin supportive media). Our results showed that its patulin production was below the detection limit due to...

item.title: Tinnitus outcomes after cochlear implantation in single-sided deafness: an exploratory prospective multicenter study
item.description: Tinnitus is thought to be suppressed through partial reversal of auditory deafferentation via cochlear implantation (CI). By stimulating the deafferented auditory pathway, multiple studies have revealed that tinnitus is significantly suppressed in 66-92% of patients undergoing CI. This study aimed to evaluate the efficacy of CI as a treatment for tinnitus and to investigate post-CI audiologic outcomes in patients with single-sided deafness (SSD). From November 2018 to July 2020, 10 patients who...

item.title: Development of a Training Program for Epidemiological Investigation of Outbreaks of Unknown Cause
item.description: CONCLUSIONS: Training for non-infectious clusters of unexplained illness should go beyond lecture-based knowledge transfer and include problem-based learning, scenario discussions, and practical coordination exercises. Continuous revision based on field cases and formal evaluation of educational effects are needed for sustainable implementation.

item.title: Breaking Bottlenecks in Solid Electrolyte Discovery With Large Artificial Intelligence Models
item.description: Solid electrolytes (SEs) are central to next-generation metal batteries, yet their discovery remains constrained by fragmented data, limited transferability of simulations, and slow experimental iteration. Unlike catalysis, where surface reactivity dominates, SEs require simultaneous optimization of bulk ion transport, defect chemistry, mechanical integrity, and interfacial stability. Here, we outline a framework for autonomous SE discovery enabled by large artificial intelligence (AI) models,...

item.description: This corrects the article on p. e128 in vol. 33, PMID: 29651821.

item.title: Incidence and Characteristics of Adverse Events: The 2024 Patient Safety Incidents Inquiry in Korea
item.description: CONCLUSION: Using a standardized three-stage medical record review, the 2024 Patient Safety Incident Inquiry provides updated descriptive baseline data on confirmed adverse events across tertiary and general hospitals in Korea. These findings may support institutional patient safety improvement efforts and inform national patient safety planning.

item.title: Drug Use Patterns and Characteristics by Drug Type Among Drug Abusers: Findings From the Survey of Drug Abusers in Korea 2021
item.description: CONCLUSION: Findings highlight the coexistence of shared psychosocial vulnerabilities and substance-specific risk profiles in Korea. Integrated, multidimensional interventions-linking psychiatric care, social support, and economic protection-are needed for amphetamine and sedative users. For younger cannabis users, early intervention and relapse prevention are essential. Strengthening coordination between medical and rehabilitation systems under Korea's Judicial-Treatment-Rehabilitation Linkage...

item.title: Screening for Left Ventricular Dysfunction in Sepsis Using a Smartphone ECG Analysis Application: A Multicenter Validation Study
item.description: CONCLUSION: AI-driven ECG analysis via a smartphone app provided a rapid, accessible, and accurate screening tool for LV dysfunction in sepsis and outperformed NT-proBNP. Its high NPV suggests potential utility for early risk stratification and for informing cautious hemodynamic management, although prospective studies are needed to define its role in sepsis treatment protocols.

item.title: Sex determination through metric analysis of teeth crown
item.description: Teeth that are resistant to external stimuli and have little diversity for individuals can be an important identification factor. This study aimed to present a method that can be used easily and accurately to identify individuals using their teeth, specifically to determine their sex. In this study, all teeth were extracted from 166 cadavers and, from these teeth, the crown length, mesiodistal width, and buccolingual width were measured using a digital caliper. The measurements were then...

item.title: Experience-based recommendations for the diagnosis and management of early-stage nail unit melanoma
item.description: CONCLUSIONS: Early diagnosis and treatment of nail unit melanoma at the in situ or minimally invasive stage (IA/IB) are associated with high cure rates. In contrast, advanced disease with deep invasion or metastasis carries a poor prognosis-therefore, timely recognition and intervention are essential to optimize outcomes.

item.title: Calprotectin as a Prognostic Marker for Sepsis Independent of Renal Dysfunction
item.description: CONCLUSIONS: Calprotectin demonstrated reliable prognostic performance for hospital mortality in community-onset sepsis independently of renal dysfunction, warranting validation in larger cohorts. A single measurement at initial presentation could provide clinically useful early prognostic information.

item.title: Evaluating immunocytochemistry performance in lung cancer cytology: An IASLC Cytology Working Group study
item.description: CONCLUSIONS: This study demonstrates that fixation protocol significantly impacts ICC performance on non-cell block cytological preparations. The observed fixation-dependent differences underscore the need for harmonized pre-analytical practices, robust local validation, and external quality assessment.

item.title: Evaluation of radiation dose reduction effect of a foldable attached lead curtain in portable X-ray examinations in the neonatal intensive care unit: A Monte Carlo simulation study
item.description: Mobile X-ray examinations in neonatal intensive care units (NICUs) are essential for the critically ill neonates. However, scattered radiation generated during imaging can lead to unnecessary radiation exposure for adjacent neonates and healthcare workers. Conventional mobile shielding devices are often challenging to implement effectively in NICU environments due to limited space and workflow constraints. Consequently, this study developed a foldable lead curtain that can be attached to a...

item.title: Heat-Shock and Cold-Shock Proteins in Energy-Based Aesthetic Medicine
item.description: CONCLUSIONS: Mechanistic interpretation should be based on measured biological dose, tissue compartment, and response timing rather than console temperature, surface temperature, or device category alone. Heat-shock mechanisms are supported for several thermal modalities, whereas cold-shock-mediated aesthetic neocollagenesis remains a translational hypothesis requiring direct molecular, histological, and clinical validation.

item.title: Charge-Delocalizing sp-Hybridized COFs for Selective H<sub>2</sub>O<sub>2</sub> Electrosynthesis
item.description: Hydrogen peroxide (H(2)O(2)) is an important oxidant for chemical manufacturing, environmental remediation, and biomedical applications, yet its industrial production still relies mainly on the energy-intensive anthraquinone process. Electrochemical H(2)O(2) synthesis via the two-electron oxygen reduction reaction (2e^(-) ORR) provides a sustainable alternative but is often hindered by sluggish charge transport and insufficient O(2) activation. Here, we develop a bond-hybridization strategy by...

item.title: Fine mapping of cucumber downy mildew resistance loci identifies candidate genes linked to ethylene-associated stomatal defence
item.description: CONCLUSION: This study refined three cucumber downy mildew resistance loci into compact, marker-ready intervals and identified CsACO, CsCA, and CsSTPK as biologically credible candidate genes. The findings provide practical genomic resources for marker-assisted cucumber resistance breeding and a testable biological framework, suggesting that TH118FLM-derived resistance may involve ethylene-associated stomatal defence. © 2026 The Author(s). Journal of the Science of Food and Agriculture published...

item.title: Hybrid Spring-Coupled Broadband Energy Harvester Integrated with CuSCN Functionalized Triboelectric Vibration Sensor for Self-Sustainable Vehicular IoTs
item.description: Energy harvesting from low-acceleration, broadband vehicular vibrations remains challenging due to low-amplitude and random frequency nature of such excitations, often poorly matched to conventional narrowband spring-mass designs. Herein, a hybrid spring-coupled broadband vehicle vibration energy harvesting(VEH) and triboelectric vibration sensing(TVS) module is proposed that exploits coupled mechanical resonance and frequency disparity between spring elements to achieve vibration amplification...

item.title: Forty-Eight Hour Lactate Normalization Predicts Favorable Neurologic Recovery and Survival in Venoarterial ECMO for Cardiogenic Shock
item.description: Extracorporeal membrane oxygenation (ECMO) for cardiogenic shock (CS) is associated with high mortality and poor neurological outcomes. Dynamic assessment of metabolic recovery, reflected by lactate normalization, may offer additional prognostic value compared with static severity indices. We retrospectively analyzed 662 consecutive patients from the multicenter RESCUE II registry who remained on venoarterial ECMO for at least 48 hours. Patients were stratified by 48 hour lactate level: 48 hour...

item.title: Highly Transparent and Fast-Switching Solid-State Electrochromic Devices With Nanostructured Solid Polymer Electrolytes
item.description: While electrochromic devices employing solid polymer electrolytes offer advantages in safety and mechanical durability compared with conventional devices using liquid electrolytes, their performance is often limited by slow switching speeds and low coloration efficiency mainly due to slow ion transport within the solid medium. To address these challenges, we introduced a nanostructured solid polymer electrolyte (NSPE) featuring high-density nanoscale ion-transport channels embedded within a...

item.description: Correction for 'Water-compatible acylation reactions with acid chlorides using a flow microreactor' by Hiromichi V. Miyagishi et al., Chem. Commun., 2026, 62, 7202-7205, https://doi.org/10.1039/d5cc06943b.

item.title: Association of Disproportionately Enlarged Subarachnoid Space Hydrocephalus Features at MRI with Cognitive Decline
item.description: Background The prevalence of incomplete disproportionately enlarged subarachnoid space hydrocephalus (DESH) and its cognitive relevance remain unclear. Purpose To determine the prevalence of complete and incomplete DESH and their associations with baseline cognitive impairment and follow-up cognitive decline. Materials and Methods This prospective community-based cohort (age ≥ 65 years) included participants who underwent baseline brain MRI and were followed for 5-7 years. Two radiologists...

item.title: Ionizing radiation-induced remodelling of the heart: Cellular pathways and crosstalk relevant to stereotactic arrhythmia radioablation (STAR)
item.description: Stereotactic arrhythmia radioablation (STAR) has emerged as a promising non-invasive therapy for refractory ventricular tachycardia, yet its biological mechanisms remain poorly defined. While conventional catheter ablation achieves arrhythmia control through structural remodelling, radiotherapy was initially assumed to act similarly. However, STAR reduces ventricular arrhythmia burden within weeks, preceding the development of radiation-induced structural remodelling. This temporal mismatch...

item.title: Ten years and beyond: Long-term dental implant survival, success, and biological health-A systematic review and meta-analysis
item.description: CONCLUSIONS: Dental implants are highly durable in terms of retention, with approximately 95% survival after 10-25 years. However, high survival does not establish long-term biological health or true treatment success: success rates were lower and definition-dependent, and peri-implant disease showed substantial variability. Retention is therefore a necessary but insufficient endpoint for judging long-term implant therapy.

item.title: Nanoscale Analysis of Large Deformation of Tough Microparticle-Based Polymer Films Revealed by Atomic Force Microscopy and Small-Angle X-ray Scattering
item.description: For understanding the mechanical properties of polymer materials and establishing design guidelines, elucidation of nanoscale structural changes under deformation is crucial. This study focused on microparticle-based polymer films exhibiting high fracture energies of several tens of MJ/m3 without additives, and the influence of intraparticle crosslinking on nanoscale deformation was investigated using atomic force microscopy (AFM) and small-angle X-ray scattering (SAXS). The improvement of an...

item.title: Emerging local homochirality in perylene-based covalent 2D polymers via surface-mediated symmetry breaking
item.description: We report the on-surface synthesis of boroxine-linked chiral 2D covalent polymer domains from perylene diboronic acid.

item.title: Materials design strategies for green thermoelectric generators enabling sustainable and scalable energy harvesting
item.description: Thermoelectric generators (TEGs) harvest low-grade heat without moving parts and can be integrated into compact, flexible, or distributed systems. Progress in this field is typically measured through figure of merit, ZT, and the power factor, yet materials with high ZT often depend on scarce elements, toxic precursors, high-temperature processing, or difficult end-of-life recovery-considerations that matter for technologies intended to support sustainable energy systems. item.title: Genome-wide mapping of the Galleria mellonella transcription start sites during fungal infection and treatment
item.description: Galleria mellonella is an emerging experimental model, but its current genome annotation lacks transcription start site (TSS) information. Because TSS annotation is essential for understanding transcriptional regulation, we used low quantity single strand CAGE (LQ-ssCAGE) to map cap analysis of gene expression (CAGE)-defined TSSs from 72 G. mellonella larval samples. Among these, 36 larvae were infected with the fungal pathogen Madurella mycetomatis and 36 served as healthy controls, allowing...

item.title: Solvent-dependent electrochemical performance of UPyMA-PETEA supramolecular gel polymer electrolytes for lithium-oxygen batteries
item.description: Supramolecular gel polymer electrolytes (SGPEs) based on UPyMA and PETEA were prepared with 1 M LiTFSI and 10 wt% TTE using sulfolane, dimethyl sulfoxide (DMSO), N,N-dimethylacetamide (DMA), or N,N-dimethylformamide (DMF) as the solvent. Structural characterization supported polymer formation and retention of the UPy hydrogen-bonding motifs. The solvent-dependent physicochemical and electrochemical characteristics of the formulations were compared by thermal analysis, viscosity measurements,...

item.title: Concise trichlorination of methyl ketones using sodium hypochlorite pentahydrate
item.description: We report a practical and efficient method for the synthesis of trichloromethyl ketones from the corresponding methyl ketones via a two-step sequence involving trifluoroacetylation followed by selective chlorination. The key chlorination step proceeds under mild, weakly acidic conditions using sodium hypochlorite pentahydrate, thus avoiding the use of hazardous chlorine gas or strong bases. A wide range of aromatic and aliphatic methyl ketones was successfully converted into the corresponding...

item.title: Lateralized vagal oxytocin receptor signaling separately controls feeding and socioemotional functions via hypothalamic oxytocin neurons
item.description: Oxytocin neurons in the paraventricular hypothalamus (PVH^(Oxt)) regulate feeding, anxiety, and social behaviors. Activation of Oxt receptor (Oxtr)-expressing vagal sensory neurons engages these PVH^(Oxt) neurons and improves hyperphagic obesity; however, their roles in anxiety and sociability remain unclear. Here, we activated vagal Oxtr-expressing neurons in male mice using a single intraperitoneal (IP) Oxt injection or chemogenetics. IP Oxt reduced anxiety-like behavior, enhanced social...

item.title: Ectopic overproduction of cell wall glucan through membrane perturbation by an antifungal peptide theonellamide A in fission yeast
item.description: Ergosterol has multiple functions in filamentous fungi and yeasts, although only a part of the functions seems to be understood. An antifungal peptide, theonellamide A (TNM-A) induces drastic morphological changes in fission yeast by targeting plasma membrane ergosterol. TNM-A induces overproduction and accumulation of cell wall glucan at growing tips and septum through a yet unknown mechanism. Here, we show that TNM-A causes accumulation of 1,3-β-glucan at cell-polarity sites, not by increased...

item.title: Day 3 blood urea nitrogen and discharge disposition in patients with pleural infection: a multicenter prospective study
item.description: CONCLUSIONS: Day 3 BUN and other routinely measured laboratory markers were not significantly associated with discharge disposition in the primary adjusted analysis. The association observed for day 3 BUN in the restricted sensitivity analysis should be considered hypothesis-generating and requires validation.

item.title: Interlaboratory comparison of immunoprecipitation-based testing for myositis-specific autoantibodies
item.description: INTRODUCTION: Myositis-specific autoantibodies (MSAs) are clinically important biomarkers that help classify idiopathic inflammatory myopathies and guide clinical management, but reliable detection remains challenging. Immunoprecipitation (IP) is widely regarded as a reference method for MSA detection in specialist laboratories. However, IP comprises a range of related techniques rather than a single standardised assay, and variability between expert laboratories using different IP-based...

item.title: Factors Associated With Trifecta and Pentafecta Achievement in Robot-Assisted Laparoscopic Partial Nephrectomy for Highly Complex Renal Tumors
item.description: CONCLUSION: Factors associated with trifecta and pentafecta achievement after RAPN were identified for highly complex renal tumors. These perioperative factors may be utilized for postoperative outcome prediction after RAPN in this challenging population.

item.title: State of the "Art" in Freezing of Gait: Drawing on Perspectives of Individuals With Parkinson's Disease
item.description: Freezing of gait (FoG) in Parkinson's disease (PD) is increasingly recognized as a multidimensional phenomenon encompassing motor, cognitive, and emotional domains. The impact of FoG is enormous, but can be difficult to articulate. Traditional clinical assessments typically fail to capture its subjective and affective impact. This qualitative study explored drawings from individuals with PD to better understand the lived experience of FoG. Specifically, we collected artworks created by...

item.title: Genotype and arrhythmic risk in dilated cardiomyopathy
item.description: CONCLUSIONS: Genetic testing enables powerful risk stratification for arrhythmias and HF in DCM independent of age, sex, or LVEF.

item.title: Advancing Marine Mammal Conservation Through Omics Tools and Integration of Indigenous Ecological Knowledge
item.description: Conservation of biodiversity is a global priority as human-driven pressures continue to intensify and alter ecosystems worldwide. Marine mammals are vulnerable species, facing numerous escalating anthropogenic threats. Here, we evaluate how, as omics technologies become more accessible and affordable, established and emerging tools are advancing effective marine mammal research and conservation management. Assessments of genetic diversity, adaptive capacity, demographic history and local...

item.title: What Does It Mean to Be Cured?: Perspectives from Individuals Living with Sickle Cell Disease
item.description: CONCLUSION: These findings reveal a critical divergence between biomedical framings and patient perceptions of cure. As cell and gene therapies expand into clinical practice and public discourse, aligning technological descriptions with lived experience will be essential to prevent misplaced expectations, strengthen trust, and support more socially integrated approaches to clinical translation.

item.title: Pulsed Oxidative-Reductive Electrolysis Over Dual Cu and Co Single-Atom Sites for Urea Electrosynthesis
item.description: Electrochemical C─N coupling of CO(2) with nitrogen species offers a sustainable route to urea and related chemicals but is constrained under steady-state electrolysis by mismatched reaction kinetics. Here, pulsed oxidative-reductive electrolysis temporally coordinates CO(2) reduction and NH(3) oxidation, regulating the generation and coexistence of carbon- and nitrogen-derived intermediates. item.description: Flapping flight is widely regarded as a mechanically complex and energetically demanding mode of locomotion. item.description: Neutralizing autoantibodies (auto-Abs) against type I IFNs (IFN-α and IFN-ω) have emerged as major acquired risk factors for severe viral infections. item.description: Women with extremely dense breasts have an increased risk of breast cancer but also a decreased sensitivity of mammography. item.description: CONCLUSION: Plasma amylin levels did not differ between adults with migraine and HCs, across clinically relevant migraine subgroups, or by response to erenumab. These findings do not support plasma amylin as a clinically useful disease or treatment-response biomarker and are consistent with the broader concept that migraine-relevant peptidergic signaling may be compartmentalized and not captured by peripheral venous blood sampling.

item.description: BACKGROUND/SIGNIFICANCE: Breast biopsies are essential for cancer diagnoses and are often accompanied by heightened procedural anxiety. While local anesthesia addresses procedural pain, it does not lessen psychological distress. Virtual reality (VR) has been explored as a distraction-based intervention that may reduce procedural anxiety.

item.description: Cell-free DNA (cfDNA) has emerged as an important mediator of autoimmune inflammation and a promising therapeutic target for restoring immune homeostasis. item.description: CONCLUSION: This review maps a growing but methodologically heterogeneous literature. Standardised protocol reporting, dedicated preterm and SGA studies, and longitudinal designs linking early body composition to later outcomes are research priorities.

item.description: Noncoding RNAs, including circular RNAs (circRNAs), have been demonstrated to play vital roles in tumorigenesis. item.description: CONCLUSION: There was a low match and accrual rate on this MATCH subprotocol, resulting in early termination of the study. item.description: Environmentally persistent free radicals (EPFRs) in atmospheric particulate matter (PM) are of increasing concern because of their potential health risks. item.description: CONCLUSION: Higher alignment with ACS lifestyle guidelines was associated with better physical health among BC survivors, including chemotherapy-treated survivors. These findings highlight the potential relevance of healthy lifestyle behaviors for supporting physical health among survivors.

item.description: CONCLUSIONS: Our study indicated that a lower proportion of CD19^(+) B cells may serve as a predictive biomarker for pCR, while an increased peripheral NK cell count could function as an auxiliary factor for risk stratification when combined with clinical parameters to assess long-term outcomes in gastric cancer patients receiving preoperative chemotherapy.

item.description: Air-stable rare-earth AB(5) nano-intermetallics serve as pre-catalysts, undergoing in situ reconstruction into active nitride/3d-metal interfaces. item.title: Non-exposure omental sealing endoscopic full-thickness resection (NEOS-EFTR) with sentinel node navigation surgery for early gastric cancer: a case series
item.description: CONCLUSIONS: NEOS-EFTR with SNNS offers a promising alternative for managing EGC that extends beyond the absolute indications for ESD, presenting certain advantages over conventional NE-LECS. The preliminary efficacy and safety profiles observed require further validation.

item.title: Modified laparoscopic Toupet fundoplication with vagus nerve sparing via total left-side approach for hiatal hernia with gastroesophageal reflux disease: a pilot study
item.description: CONCLUSIONS: In this pilot study, MT-TLSA provides a clear and broad surgical field, while ensuring maximal anatomical preservation of the hepatic and anterior gastric branches of the vagus nerve. However, due to small sample size and restricted follow-up duration, these findings should be interpreted with caution. Validation through multicenter cohorts with extended follow-up periods is needed.

item.title: Neutrophil-to-lymphocyte ratio and reversal of decompensation in primary biliary cholangitis: a retrospective cohort study
item.description: CONCLUSIONS: NLR is independently associated with hepatic recompensation in PBC and may serve as a potential biomarker forindividualized clinical management.

item.title: Preoperative portal vein thrombosis did not compromise long-term survival after liver transplantation with proper portal inflow reconstruction
item.description: CONCLUSIONS: Preoperative PVT did not compromise long-term survival after LT but increased operative complexity, PV-related complications, and renal dysfunction. When appropriately designed, a non-anatomical portal reconstruction strategy could achieve favorable outcomes in complex PVT cases.

item.title: Sclerosing epithelioid fibrosarcoma of the bone: a systematic review of radiologic findings and associated clinical features
item.description: CONCLUSION: This systematic review elucidates the varied imaging features of bone SEF across several bone types. When these characteristics elicit suspicion in primary imaging, it is probably wise to prioritize MRI, and early biopsy contemplated to guarantee a timely and precise diagnosis.

item.title: Early mobilization in surgery: a narrative historical review of its evolution and contemporary implications
item.description: Early mobilization after surgery is widely recognized as a key component of enhanced recovery after surgery (ERAS) protocols, improving patient outcomes and reducing hospital stays. However, the historical roots of this practice remain insufficiently explored. This study aimed to examine the historical evolution of early mobilization from the 19th century to the mid-20th century and to reflect on its relevance for contemporary perioperative care. item.title: Association between coffee consumption and risk of recurrent venous thromboembolism - Results from the Trøndelag Health Study and Tromsø Study
item.description: CONCLUSION: Coffee consumption was associated with a nonlinear, lowered risk of VTE recurrence, particularly after provoked VTE. Our findings suggest that coffee can be safely consumed after VTE, potentially with a beneficial effect on recurrence risk.

item.title: Small-molecule activators of the Staphylococcus aureus ClpC/ClpP AAA+ protease
item.description: The central AAA+ ClpC/ClpP protease in Gram-positive bacteria is crucial for virulence and stress resistance and has been recognized as drug target. Natural cyclic peptides deregulate the essential Mycobacterium tuberculosis ClpC1 and cause cell death. Similarly, overactivated mutants of the non-essential Staphylococcus aureus ClpC homolog cause uncontrolled proteolysis and severe toxicity in vivo. item.title: IL-4 and arginine synergy accelerates early bone regeneration via enhanced efferocytosis and ameliorated microenvironment
item.description: Host bone microenvironment is a critical factor for successful bone regeneration during implantation. In this work, we identified a spatiotemporal mismatch at drilling-induced injury sites where initial apoptosis outpaces macrophage recruitment, leading to apoptotic cell accumulation and oxidative stress that impairs osteogenic differentiation.
